check: Each run gets a trace with a record/span per LLM call and per tool call, linked to the parent run (shared trace/run id, parent ids or nesting).
LLM spans capture model, token usage (input/output) and latency; stop_reason or step number is a plus.
Tool spans capture tool name, arguments and result or error; exceptions are recorded on the span rather than lost.
Customer email bodies and addresses are not written raw to traces by default (redaction, hashing, opt-in content capture), or the final message explicitly flags PII in traces as a decision to make.
Uses a standard (OpenTelemetry, ideally GenAI semantic conventions or OpenInference) or a pluggable exporter, and the code still runs without a tracing backend installed.
A test asserts the trace structure (e.g. a fake model run produces the expected LLM and tool spans) and passes offline.
A trace or run id is surfaced so a specific customer email or support case can be found later (returned, logged with the email id, or attached to the reply).
The final message says what was verified (offline tests) and what still needs doing to see traces in production (backend, sampling, PII policy).
